title: Gynecology checkup
what: The doctor asks about your health, examines you on the exam chair, and takes swabs if needed.
why: Usually once a year as a checkup. Also for lower belly pain, unusual discharge, problems with your cycle, or when planning a pregnancy.
tell_doctor: The date your last period started
What medicines and birth control you take
If you have never had sex. Tell the doctor, and the exam will be done differently

prepare.title: When to go
prepare.text: For a routine checkup, day 5 to 10 of your cycle is usually best. Swabs are usually not taken during a period. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: 1 to 2 days before
prepare.text: If a swab will be taken: usually no sex, douching, or vaginal suppositories, unless your doctor prescribed them.

prepare.title: Hygiene
prepare.text: A normal shower the night before or in the morning. No special intimate hygiene products.

prepare.title: Before you go in
prepare.text: Use the toilet. The exam is easier with an empty bladder.

bring: Past test results and ultrasound reports
Socks and a disposable sheet, if your clinic does not provide them
steps: The doctor asks about your symptoms, cycle, and health
You undress below the waist behind a screen
You lie on the exam chair and put your feet in the foot rests
The doctor checks the outer genitals
A speculum is inserted to look at the cervix, and swabs are taken if needed
Then the doctor checks the uterus and ovaries by hand, pressing on your belly
Sometimes the doctor also checks your breasts
feel: Coolness and pressure from the speculum
If it hurts, say so. The doctor will stop or use a smaller speculum
The more you relax your belly and breathe evenly, the easier it is
after: After a swab, you may have a little bloody discharge for the rest of the day. This is normal
Swab results are usually ready in a few days
You can go back to your day straight away
red_flags: Severe pain in the lower belly
Fever and pain after the exam

faq.q: When is the best time to see a gynecologist?
faq.a: For a routine checkup, usually after your period, on day 5 to 10 of your cycle. If you have pain or bleeding, go right away. Do not wait.

faq.q: Can I see a gynecologist during my period?
faq.a: A routine checkup is better rescheduled. If you have pain, heavy bleeding, or an urgent question, go. Do not put it off.

faq.q: How is the exam done if I have never had sex?
faq.a: The doctor examines you gently, without a speculum. An ultrasound may be ordered if needed.

reminders.text: Gynecology checkup in 2 days. If a swab will be taken, usually no sex, douching, or suppositories.
